_note: General extension guidance (ICAR / state agricultural universities). Not a prescription: confirm with your KVK / Krishi officer and follow the product label dose.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.symptoms: No disease signs found on this leaf.
healthy.prevention: Keep checking leaves every week, water at the base and keep the field clean.

Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple scab
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves; cracked, scabby fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungus (Venturia inaequalis), spreads in cool wet weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Spray captan or mancozeb as per label every 7–10 days in wet weather. Remove badly infected leaves.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Destroy fallen leaves, prune for air flow, plant resistant varieties.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple black rot
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-edged 'frog-eye' spots on leaves, black rotting fruit, cankers on branches.
Apple___Black_rot.cause: Fungus (Botryosphaeria obtusa) living in dead wood and dried fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Cut out cankers and dead wood; spray captan or copper fungicide as per label.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove dried fruit and dead branches, avoid wounds on trees.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar apple rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on the upper leaf; small tubes under the leaf later.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Rust fungus that needs juniper/cedar trees nearby.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Spray mancozeb or myclobutanil as per label from pink-bud stage in wet weather.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby juniper trees if possible; plant resistant varieties.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.name: Cherry powdery mildew
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powder on young leaves; leaves curl and twist.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus favoured by warm days and humid nights.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray wettable sulphur or a recommended fungicide as per label.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Prune for air flow, avoid too much nitrogen, remove infected shoots.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Maize grey leaf spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long rectangular grey-brown spots between leaf veins.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Fungus (Cercospora zeae-maydis); warm humid weather and old crop residue.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: If severe before tasselling, spray azoxystrobin or propiconazole as per label.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Rotate with non-cereal crops, bury residue, grow tolerant hybrids.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Maize common rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both sides of the leaf.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Rust fungus (Puccinia sorghi); cool humid weather.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Spray mancozeb or a recommended triazole fungicide as per label if it spreads early.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Grow resistant hybrids and sow on time.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Maize northern leaf blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long (3–15 cm) grey-green cigar-shaped spots on leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Fungus (Exserohilum turcicum); mild temperature with heavy dew.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Spray mancozeb or a recommended fungicide as per label at first signs.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Resistant hybrids, crop rotation, destroy infected residue.

Grape___Black_rot.name: Grape black rot
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown leaf spots with dark edges; berries turn black and shrivel.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Spray mancozeb or a recommended fungicide as per label from early shoot growth.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove dried berries, prune to keep the canopy open.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).name: Grape esca (black measles)
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe yellowing between veins, dark spots on berries, sudden vine drying.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: Wood-rotting fungi entering through pruning cuts.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: No cure. Cut infected wood well below the symptoms and burn it.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Prune in dry weather, seal big cuts, disinfect pruning tools.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.name: Grape leaf blight
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots; leaves dry and fall early.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Spray mancozeb or copper oxychloride as per label.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Remove fallen leaves, improve air flow, avoid wetting leaves.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).name: Citrus greening (HLB)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy yellow leaves, small lopsided bitter fruit, twig dieback.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterium spread by the citrus psyllid insect.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure. Remove and destroy infected trees; control psyllids with a recommended insecticide.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Plant certified disease-free saplings and control psyllids.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.name: Peach bacterial spot
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular spots turning purple-brown; shot holes in leaves.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray a copper bactericide as per label (not during flowering).
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, use windbreaks.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Capsicum bacterial spot
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots turning brown with a yellow ring; leaves fall.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterium (Xanthomonas) spread by rain splash and infected seed.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray copper oxychloride as per label; remove badly infected plants.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seed, rotate crops, avoid overhead watering.

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato early blight
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with rings like a target on lower leaves, yellowing around them.
Potato___Early_blight.cause: Fungus (Alternaria solani); warm weather with wet and dry spells.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil as per label every 10–15 days.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation, balanced nitrogen, remove infected leaves.

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato late blight
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked patches on leaves, white mould underneath on humid mornings; tubers rot.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans; cool (10–25 °C) and very humid weather. Spreads fast by wind.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Spray mancozeb; if the disease is spreading use cymoxanil + mancozeb or metalaxyl + mancozeb as per label. Remove infected plants.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Certified seed, earth up tubers, avoid overhead watering, spray before humid spells. Warn your neighbours.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.name: Squash powdery mildew
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves and stems; leaves turn yellow and dry.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus; dry days and humid nights.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray wettable sulphur or a recommended fungicide as per label.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Resistant varieties, good spacing, remove old infected leaves.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.name: Strawberry leaf scorch
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small purple spots that join; leaves look burnt.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Remove infected leaves; spray captan or a recommended fungicide as per label.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Healthy planting material, good spacing, avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato bacterial spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves; scabby spots on fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterium (Xanthomonas); warm wet weather, infected seed.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Spray copper oxychloride as per label; remove infected leaves.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Disease-free seed, crop rotation, do not handle wet plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato early blight
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with target rings on older leaves; spots on stems.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil as per label; remove lower infected leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Mulch, stake plants, rotate crops, water at the base.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Tomato late blight
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large greasy dark patches on leaves, white mould underneath; firm brown rot on fruit.
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans; cool and very humid weather. Spreads fast.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Spray mancozeb; if spreading use cymoxanil + mancozeb as per label. Remove infected plants.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Avoid overhead watering, give spacing, spray before humid spells, warn neighbours.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Tomato leaf mould
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on top of leaves, olive-green velvet mould underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Improve ventilation; spray chlorothalonil or a recommended fungicide as per label.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Space plants, prune lower leaves, keep leaves dry.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Tomato septoria leaf spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small round spots with dark edges and grey centres on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves; spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil as per label.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch, crop rotation, avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Spider mites
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow speckles on leaves, thin webbing underneath, leaves dry.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Tiny mites (Tetranychus urticae); hot dry weather.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Spray water under the leaves; use neem oil or a recommended miticide as per label.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Avoid water stress, remove weeds, protect natural predators.

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Tomato target spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and rings on leaves, stems and fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Spray chlorothalonil or a recommended fungicide as per label.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Good air flow, remove crop debris, rotate crops.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward and turn yellow at the edges; plants stay small, few fruits.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: No cure. Remove infected plants; control whitefly with yellow sticky traps, neem oil or a recommended insecticide.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Resistant varieties, insect net in the nursery, remove weeds.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato mosaic virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern; twisted leaves; poor fruit.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Virus spread by touch, tools and infected seed.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No cure. Remove infected plants; wash hands and disinfect tools.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Certified seed, no tobacco use near plants, disinfect tools.
